lessons.correction: Strengthen your ground forces and increase production. Build a defensive structure or a unit to counter Reaper harassment.
lessons.mistake: Overcommitting to economy and technology while ignoring the Reaper threat, leaving your workers vulnerable to harassment.
lessons.recheck: Re-evaluate when you see more of the opponent's composition or when you have a stronger army.
lessons.title: Reaper Harassment Response
lessons.when: Early game, when you spot a Reaper from the opponent and your own economy is moderate with technology investment.
lessons.why: The Reaper suggests early aggression or a tech switch; defending against it prevents economic damage and prepares you for a counter.

lessons.correction: Continue strengthening your ground forces and increasing your economy. Consider adding supporting units like Marauders or Siege Tanks.
lessons.mistake: Neglecting your economy while building an army, or overcommitting to a single unit composition without adaptability.
lessons.recheck: Re-evaluate when you see the opponent's tech choices or when you are ready to push.
lessons.title: Midgame Ground Macro Mirror
lessons.when: Midgame, when both you and the opponent have ground-based armies with Marines and Reapers, and heavy economies.
lessons.why: Both players are on a similar ground macro path; strengthening army and economy helps gain an advantage in the midgame.

lessons.correction: Maintain your current development path, but be aware that the opponent is ahead. Consider building a defensive structure or a unit to counter the opponent's composition.
lessons.mistake: Engaging the opponent's army without a plan, or neglecting your economy while trying to catch up.
lessons.recheck: Re-evaluate when you have a stronger army or when you have more information about the opponent's intentions.
lessons.title: Catching Up Against a Strong Ground Army
lessons.when: Early midgame, when the opponent has a strong ground army with Marines, Reapers, and Marauders, while your own posture is underdeveloped.
lessons.why: The opponent has a strong ground army, so you need to catch up. Maintaining development while preparing a defense is the safest option.
